Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral faces the Zócalo square with its two tall bell towers. Construction continued over several centuries, so architectural features from different periods can be seen in its façades.

Inside, the space unfolds through naves, altars and side chapels. Stone architecture, historic religious art and ongoing worship bring the capital's history to life. A visit to the cathedral can easily be combined with a walk across the Zócalo and a look at the National Palace on the other side of the square.

The Zócalo offers one of the best panoramic introductions to Mexico City. The cathedral rises along the square's northern side, while the National Palace occupies the eastern side with its long façade. The open expanse between them makes it easy to understand why the city's most important events have converged here for centuries. The Zócalo's official name is Constitution Square.

The square has retained its central position since the time of ancient Tenochtitlan. After the Spanish conquest, a new political and religious centre grew around it. To see traces of both cities side by side, walk from the cathedral to the Templo Mayor archaeological site. On the square itself, it is worth comparing the façades and watching the light change on the stone throughout the day.

The Zócalo remains a major gathering place, hosting cultural events, concerts and city celebrations. On an ordinary day it can feel spacious, while on event days it fills with people. Begin your exploration of the historic centre here, choose a route into the surrounding streets and allow time to return to the square. A second look often reveals details you missed the first time.

## La Paz: Mexico's paradise city!

The idyllic capital of Baja California Sur, on the shores of the largest bay in the Gulf of California, enjoys a leisurely way of life, beautiful beaches and spectacular sunsets. A 5 km-long boulevard runs along the waterfront, lined with hotels and restaurants.

La Paz owes its beginnings to the conquistador Hernán Cortés and its former prosperity to the abundance of pearls in the coastal waters. In the 19th century, the city led the international pearl market, but by the middle of the 20th century, overharvesting had depleted the oyster beds. Today, La Paz is popular as one of the world's finest destinations for sport fishing.

## La Paz: an ideal base for exploring!

Local waters are home to marine creatures such as hammerhead sharks and giant rays. The surrounding area also offers excellent places for hiking and ecotourism, including Puerto Balandra and the Sierra de la Laguna Biosphere Reserve. La Paz has important landmarks reflecting Mexico's historical and cultural heritage, including the Cathedral of Our Lady of La Paz, the Regional Museum of Natural History and the Biblioteca de las Californias. The city also has plenty of bars, nightclubs and restaurants serving delicious seafood.

At Estancia Mimosa, a forest trail follows the Mimoso River. Wooden walkways and viewing platforms connect the waterfalls and natural pools.

On the selected itinerary, the walk includes stops by the water, swimming and a boat trip. This route complements visits to Bonito's caves and crystal-clear rivers.
